story.title: US files new torture charges against Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro and wife Cilia Flores
story.summary: The United States on Thursday charged ousted Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores with conspiracy to commit torture, adding to drug trafficking and firearms charges. Prosecutors allege detainees, including US citizens, suffered waterboarding, rape and beatings. The pair remain in US custody following a January military raid.

linkedin.title: This Week in Finance & Tech
linkedin.body:
A massive shift in entertainment just hit the headlines. Paramount has officially completed its $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The new media giant will operate under the name Skydance. David Ellison and former Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz will co-lead the entity, which now controls a massive portfolio including HBO Max, CNN, CBS News, and several major film studios.

In the world of AI, OpenAI is making adjustments to meet European Union regulations. The company announced it will add digital watermarks to all text and code generated by its models within the EU. Meanwhile, a recent Vanity Fair interview with Sam Altman faced scrutiny after an OpenAI publicist attempted to steer the conversation away when asked about a ChatGPT user's suicide.

On the consumer tech front, Google is rolling out a new feature for Gemini Live on Android called Guided Vision. It uses your phone camera to provide real-time audio descriptions of your surroundings, which could be helpful for reading fine print or navigating new spaces. Also in hardware, a company called Neurable is launching headphones that claim to track your focus levels and alert you when it is time to take a mental break.

Finally, in Brazil, markets are reacting to the ongoing presidential election. Stocks jumped following the first round of voting, as current polling suggests Jair Bolsonaro is a strong favorite heading into the October 25 runoff against incumbent Lula da Silva.

instagram.title: Nicolás Maduro Indicted on Torture Charges

slides.headline: Nicolás Maduro Indicted on Torture Charges
slides.subtitle: The former Venezuelan president has been jailed in New York since January.

slides.explanation: Maduro and his wife have been held in a New York facility since early January, marking a significant shift in their legal status on American soil.

slides.headline: They are already in US custody
slides.explanation: While many international indictments take years to process, the couple has been detained in New York for weeks before these specific torture charges were unsealed.
Six major international news organizations have independently verified these court documents, confirming the charges are consistent across global reporting.

slides.subtitle: Read the full breakdown on Headlinne.

instagram.caption:
Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, are facing serious charges in a Manhattan federal court.

The indictment focuses on allegations of conspiracy to commit torture against US citizens.

It is a rare move to see a former head of state indicted while already physically detained within the country filing the charges. The legal process is now moving forward in New York.

This case highlights the ongoing tension between Venezuelan leadership and the international legal system. We are tracking how this evolves in court.

story.title: Nicolás Maduro and his wife indicted for alleged torture of US citizens
story.summary: Ousted Venezuelan president and Cilia Flores have been in jail in New York since early January The deposed Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, have been indicted for alleged conspiracy to commit torture, according to Manhattan federal court papers unsealed on Thursday. The superseding indictment was unsealed shortly before Flores appeared at court in her ongoing push for pretrial release – which was denied by Judge Alvin Hellerstein. Maduro and Flores have been jailed in New York City since early January. Continue reading...
